classicBeybladePhysics: Classic Plastic Generation physics apply: physical Beyblades stay palm-sized, solid and tip-driven; right-spin and left-spin remain constant; stadium translation is separate from axial rotation; collisions use direct Attack Ring contact with recoil; supernatural energy remains anchored to the visible physical top. Real-world spin-stability lock: angular momentum is the only thing that keeps a free Beyblade balanced on its pointed tip. As RPM approaches zero, precession must widen, the rim or base must touch, and gravity must tip the body onto its side. A non-spinning free top may not remain upright on its tip or freeze in a balanced pose. It may stay level while not spinning only when visibly supported by a hand or fixture, lying flat on a broad surface, or firmly locked to both launcher posts.

optional_h3_storyboard_reference.prompt: {{STORYBOARD_REFERENCE}} is the storyboard reference for the mapped shots, defining their viewpoint, framing, subject placement, screen direction, and shot order. Read its visual panels sequentially, one corresponding panel per listed shot, then render exactly one ordinary full-screen moving shot at a time in the requested visual style. The storyboard sheet itself is never visible: no multi-panel grid, split screen, panel borders, divider lines, gutters, white margins, page edges, cropped fragments from adjacent panels, captions, labels, timestamps, or typography.

stadiumMotionLock: Post-landing stadium-motion lock: after the tip's first contact, a spinning Beyblade must continue both axial rotation and visible translation across the bowl. A brief landing skid transitions immediately into a curved orbit governed by tip friction, gravity and the local bowl tangent; on a slope it travels along or down the surface and may precess, climb, descend or deflect, but it never adheres to the slope, freezes in place, or pivots around a glued point. Even a defense-type top traces a tight low-speed orbit or small precessing circle. It may become stationary only after RPM decays, wobble widens, the rim scrapes and the body falls onto its side.
realWorldSpinStabilityLock: Real-world spin-stability lock: angular momentum is the only thing that keeps a free Beyblade balanced on its pointed tip. As RPM approaches zero, precession must widen, the rim or base must touch, and gravity must tip the body onto its side. A non-spinning free top may not remain upright on its tip or freeze in a balanced pose. It may stay level while not spinning only when visibly supported by a hand or fixture, lying flat on a broad surface, or firmly locked to both launcher posts.
launcherAttachmentProximityLock: Launcher-to-Beyblade proximity lock: whenever a Beyblade is loaded before release, its flat upper face is in direct visible contact with the launcher underside, with zero visible air gap. Exactly two short close-set launcher prongs are fully inserted into the paired slots beside the central Bit Chip and twist-locked together; the top is level, centered on the launcher axis, and its tip points straight down. The launcher and loaded top move as one rigid assembly with identical position and tilt: no dangling top, long connector, exposed suspension gap, single-post support, floating, or early separation. The visible gap begins only on the single release frame, when both prongs disengage together and the already-spinning top immediately descends tip-first under gravity.
launcherNoConnectorLock: Launcher silhouette lock: the Beyblade's upper face sits immediately beneath and touches the actual launcher housing. Only the two very short engagement prongs hidden inside the top's center slots may connect them. Never draw any long black rod, vertical shaft, stem, axle, neck, cable, string, spacer, tether, suspension bar, or extended post between launcher and Beyblade.
dialogueTurnPolicy: Exactly one named structured speaker owns each timed line; all other visible humans keep lips closed for that interval.
